newsitem.title: UK: Brent gains more ground but grades seen peaking.
newsitem.headline: Brent gains more ground but grades seen peaking.

text.p: Brent crude oil continued to gain ground on Tuesday but most other North Sea grades were felt to have reached their current peak, traders said.
A cargo of Brent loading May 6-8 sold on Tuesday at June Brent -31 cents, up from Monday's June -37 cent trade as one buyer continued to purchase for a VLCC destined for the U.S., traders said.
The single Brent cargo which turned wet on Tuesday was taken before the five o' clock deadline by British Petroleum.
Traders said loadings of Gullfaks A crude were delayed 2-3 days due to problems at the Vigdis field.
The only other grade to show upward potential was Forties which traded on Tuesday at around dated Brent +22 cents.
Ekofisk eased back from recent deals at Dated Brent +15 cents to move at Dated +13 cents for a 15-17 loader.
June Brent on the IPE futures gained some 33 cents by 1725 GMT to trade at $18.60 a barrel.

CFDs and intermonth spreads were active over the day. Good buying on the prompt CFD market led to narrower spreads and late talk on the remainder of this week (April 29-02) saw buyers at June Brent -31 cents while sellers held off three cents higher.
Brent intermonth spreads tightened with May/June trading as high as -21 cents while Jun/Jul narrowed from an early -13 cents to later deals at -10 cents.
Although Urals buyers in the Mediterranean were thin, the limited volumes of the crude on offer should hold prices steady to firmer, traders said.
Two large cargoes were offered at dated Brent -90 cents and most agreed the market level was around dated -95 cents.
West African markets were similarly steady with sellers waiting to see if Eastern buying demand continues. Current tightening of the Brent/Dubai spread was thought temporary,
